issues.acceptance: A representative native-renderer before/after capture reports raw frame times, one-percent low, hitch count, CPU/GPU attribution, and named script hot paths with 3, 5, 10, and 18 active enemies. Enemy separation is computed once from a cached stable roster per physics cycle, QA instrumentation performs no per-frame deep state snapshot or scene-wide scan in ordinary play, and AI behavior/spacing remains unchanged. llvmpipe evidence is recorded only as collector evidence.
issues.actual: scripts/enemy_agent.gd rebuilds and sorts the complete fusepoint_enemy group inside _separation_safe_velocity(), then invokes that admission path multiple times per navigation cycle for every active enemy. At the same time, the main scene runs RuntimeQualificationProbe in PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS, deep-calls mission/roster/weapon state and periodically scans the complete scene tree for audio players. With 18 active enemies these are credible CPU hitch hot paths and must be profiled on a native renderer; the llvmpipe collector result cannot attribute the user's stutter to their computer.
issues.expected: Ordinary gameplay performs bounded enemy steering and lightweight production work per frame; deep QA snapshots run only on demand or at a bounded debug sampling cadence.
issues.next_action: Capture native-renderer CPU/GPU profiler evidence, remove duplicate peer scans and sorts, and gate or sample QA-only deep observation.

blocking_focus: Complete the candidate-bound Tester MCP state matrix.

preservation_constraints.requirement: Keep frozen technical baseline `clean_boot` passing. Do not treat this as a mandate to preserve the same visible asset, map, HUD family, or material choice if a higher-quality replacement is available and the PRD still fits.

task_specification.objective: Make the three active combat-readability issues closure-ready by separating terminal bomb failure from ordinary death recovery, synchronizing combat feedback to immutable events through Alpha/Bravo encounters, and qualifying/removing candidate-owned runtime hot paths without lowering visual, combat, map, or weapon fidelity.

diagnosis.root_cause: Loop 76 is in convergence mode with three host-selected active issues. Prior evidence shows one hard terminal-routing defect where countdown-zero/bomb_detonated correctly commits mission state and health zero, but ProductShell then treats that terminal failure as ordinary combat death, pauses the tree, and stalls the failure presentation. The combat feedback issue is not closure-ready because Alpha/Bravo combat transitions still lack a same-event, same-frame-or-two-frame chain from authoritative shot/damage/kill/objective records into HUD/audio/VFX without duplicate cleanup/presentation. The performance issue remains unqualified because prior checks did not isolate product hot paths from renderer or MCP overhead across ordinary combat and finale lifecycle states; the likely candidate-owned risk is unbounded per-frame diagnostics/snapshots, enemy roster/avoidance work, audio/VFX churn, or scene/runtime scans during active play rather than a render-quality setting.

stop_conditions: Do not modify frozen product context, run-control evidence, imported read-only source assets, or accepted AK-74M viewmodel component assets/audio/profile values.
Do not treat fresh host recapture, broad QA matrix generation, or software-renderer-only profiling as the implementation itself; candidate changes must make Tester recapture possible and meaningful.

Do not collapse deferred issues into current-loop task disposition; keep enemy animation, weapon report audio, story cue, and separate runtime-stutter debt visible only through validation patrol unless the implementation directly touches them.
Do not lower resolution, render scale, lighting/exposure, map density, enemy count, VFX fidelity, or simulation coverage to pass performance.
Stop and report if the required terminal failure, combat feedback, or performance surfaces are owned only by unavailable external harness code rather than candidate-owned scripts/resources.

strategy.rationale: Use a materially different root-cause strategy from repeated tuning: repair authoritative state routing and latches first, then bind feedback and performance evidence to immutable runtime events and named hot paths. This targets three closure-ready active issues while preserving the accepted golden path, controls, weapon component, and authored map baseline.

code: Run Godot/GDScript syntax/import validation for all changed candidate scripts and resources.
Inspect changed-path signal connections so terminal, mission, player death, HUD, combat feedback, and runtime qualification observers do not create duplicate event submissions.
Confirm no accepted read-only AK-74M component source audio/profile/transform files or frozen run evidence files were modified.
runtime: Clean boot preservation: title/home -> loadout -> briefing -> deployment -> gameplay with movement, mouse yaw/pitch, reload on R, pause/resume, and F6 recovery still working.

Bomb finale retest: ordinary gameplay smoke, then tester_terminal_failure_prepare, screenshot/runtime state, tester_terminal_failure_advance, step through terminal failure presentation, verify no death_recovery diversion, failure_result retry/home, logs clean; repeat success branch smoke to preserve bomb_defused routing.

Combat feedback retest: Alpha and Bravo prepared or ordinary encounters covering player shot miss, player hit, enemy damage to player, enemy kill/death, objective transition, checkpoint restore, F6, Replay; compare event ids across state, HUD, audio/VFX receipts, cleanup receipts, and screenshots.

Performance retest: native 1920x1080 gl_compatibility run with ordinary combat route at 3/5/10/18 enemies and bomb detonation window; capture frame-time distribution, named hot paths, active node/process/audio/VFX counts, and three restart/replay lifecycle cycles without fatal logs.
visual: Compare gameplay HUD frames against the PRD effect-imagination reference hierarchy: top-left minimap, top-center countdown/compass, restrained top-right combat feed, center-lower objective band, lower-left vitals, lower-right weapon state, and borderless subtitle/radio text without reticle or enemy occlusion.
Capture terminal failure presentation and final failure result frames to prove the bomb-detonation path is visually distinct from ordinary operator-down recovery.

Run one bounded FPS regression patrol for changed-adjacent surfaces: movement/mouse/reload/F6 lifecycle, weapon recoil return, quick AUTO/SEMI audio ownership state where touched, enemy occupancy/causal shots where touched, HUD safe area at 100 percent and 200 percent UI scale, and late runtime errors.

done_when: Countdown-zero or tester_terminal_failure_prepare followed by tester_terminal_failure_advance commits exactly one bomb_detonated terminal event, sets player health to zero once, disables combat once, and never enters ProductShell death_recovery or recovery_transition before the bomb failure result is complete.

TerminalPresentation failure branch advances while the tree is not paused by ordinary death recovery; elapsed_seconds increases, completion_count reaches 1, and ProductShell routes through detonation/failure_result with retry and home actions exposed.
Ordinary combat death still enters the grayscale death recovery/checkpoint restart branch, and existing terminal success routing to victory/success_result remains preserved.

Tester-facing prepare and advance actions remain debug-only, have no physical release binding, produce requested/resolved/reset-isolation receipts, and separate stable failure preparation from failure advancement.

Runtime state and screenshot evidence can show mission_state=bomb_detonated, terminal_commit_count=1, app_state=failure_result or active terminal failure presentation, health=0, and no generic operator-down recovery page on the bomb detonation path.
tasks.instructions: Repair the ProductShell/MissionController/TerminalPresentation lifecycle so terminal bomb failure has priority over ordinary player-death recovery. Audit the terminal_submitted, player death, tree pause, page transition, and tester_terminal_failure_* paths for shared health-zero latches. Gate ordinary death recovery on non-terminal combat death, clear or ignore death-recovery latches for authoritative bomb_detonated, and keep the terminal failure presentation advancing until it emits completion and lands on the failure result page. Preserve the previously verified success path and ordinary restart behavior.
tasks.title: Separate Bomb Failure From Ordinary Death

done_when: Alpha and Bravo encounter transitions each expose at least one ordinary or deterministic prepared player shot, enemy shot/damage event, kill/death event, and objective event with immutable event_id or shot_id shared by HUD row, reticle/world feedback, audio/VFX receipt, and mission/combat state.
Combat feed contains at most five restrained rows and presents no duplicate row, stale cleanup callback, bare debug label, or generic floating Enemy killed text for the same immutable event.

Player damage feedback uses the authoritative damage event, updates health/vitals and bounded red directional arc within two rendered frames, and blocked/missed enemy shots produce no damage or red hit feedback.

Shot/impact/kill feedback remains synchronized for both Alpha and Bravo after checkpoint restore, F6 reset, Replay, and one lifecycle cleanup pass; cleanup receipts show no duplicate cleanup callbacks or orphaned feedback nodes/audio players.

If ordinary route coverage is too long, debug-only tester encounter prepare/advance actions stop in stable inspectable Alpha/Bravo states and do not immediately kill, capture, or resolve the objective.

tasks.title: Synchronize Alpha Bravo Combat Feedback

done_when: Runtime qualification reports startup renderer as the registered gl_compatibility backend, 3D render scale remains 1.0 at 1920x1080, and no performance fix changes map lighting/exposure, enemy count, weapon component fidelity, VFX fidelity, or simulation coverage.

Candidate-owned profiling or runtime_qualification output names CPU/GPU frame time, raw frame-time samples, one-percent low, hitch timestamps, active enemies, audio voice counts, transient VFX counts, and named script hot paths for ordinary gameplay at 3, 5, 10, and 18 enemies plus the bomb detonation window.

Any product hot path found in per-frame diagnostics, HUD snapshots, enemy peer scans, route reservations, navigation callbacks, audio/VFX spawning, or scene-tree polling is bounded, cached, sampled, pooled, or made debug-only without removing required gameplay feedback.

Explosion/failure presentation does not remain below 45 FPS for three consecutive frames on the qualified target route, and restart/replay/home cycles run three times without state drift, orphaned audio/VFX, fatal script errors, or growing active node/process counts.

If native hardware/runtime collector remains unavailable, Developer still leaves candidate-owned instrumentation and receipts in place and explicitly separates unqualified external evidence from completed source/runtime hot-path repairs.
